Earlier this year in March, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro, confirming it had no plans to release any new Mac Pro hardware.

Bloomberg published a report today, further revealing the story behind Apple’s Mac Pro strategy, including an unexpected detail…

The inside story of Apple shelving the Mac Pro

In the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Mark Gurman noted that Apple internally had "no intention of giving up on the Mac Pro from the start." Gurman revisited an earlier claim: Apple had originally planned to release a chip named "Extreme" on top of its "Ultra" chips.

The report quoted: "Apple was developing two chips at the time, the M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme, but ultimately shelved the project due to considerations of cost and demand."

As for the already-developed Mac Pro hardware, Gurman said Apple had two models (internal codenames J170 and J190) in development, but neither was ever brought to market.

The most intriguing detail in the report is that one of the models used an Intel processor:

Apple finally officially discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removing it from its official website and directing buyers to the Mac Studio instead. Although the discontinuation was long anticipated, for Mac Pro supporters it still marks the quiet end of an era.

Apple has abandoned the Mac Pro product line, and chosen not to release an "Extreme" chip in the Apple Silicon era. What do you think of this decision? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
